fullPassage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for recognizing our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be transmitted is which button to push — essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that contribute to a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.

questions.passage: Herbert Simon won his Nobel Prize for (A)[recognizing / ignoring] our limitations in information, time, and cognitive capacity. As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the population and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation. Then all we have to do is socially learn the right answers. You don't need to understand how your computer or toilet works; you just need to be able to use the interface and flush. All that needs to be (B)[transmitted / concealed] is which button to push — essentially how to interact with technologies rather than how they work. And so instead of holding more information than we have mental capacity for and indeed need to know, we could dedicate our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation. We understand things well enough to benefit from them, but all the while we are making small calculations that (C)[contribute to / detract from] a larger whole. We are just doing our part in a larger computation for our societies' collective brains.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ② recognizing — transmitted — contribute to: 원문 일치. Simon은 인간의 한계를 인식했고(recognizing), 전달되어야 할(transmitted) 것은 버튼을 누르는 법이며, 작은 계산이 더 큰 전체에 기여한다(contribute to)는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ① ignoring — transmitted — contribute to: (A) ignoring(무시하다)은 recognizing(인식하다)의 반의어
❌ ③ recognizing — concealed — contribute to: (B) concealed(숨기다)는 transmitted(전달하다)의 반의어
❌ ④ ignoring — concealed — detract from: 3개 모두 오류
det.tip: recognizing our limitations(한계를 인식) / needs to be transmitted(전달되어야 하는) / contribute to a larger whole(더 큰 전체에 기여)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

❌ ① possess — interface — dedicate: (A) possess(소유하다)는 lack(부족하다)의 반의어
❌ ② lack — mechanism — dedicate: (B) mechanism(작동 원리)은 interface(인터페이스)와 다른 의미
✅ ③ lack — interface — dedicate: 원문 일치. 자원이 부족하고(lack), 인터페이스(interface)를 사용할 줄만 알면 되며, 큰 두뇌를 작은 계산에 바친다(dedicate)는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ lack — interface — expose: (C) expose(노출하다)는 dedicate(바치다)와 다른 의미
det.tip: lack the resources(자원이 부족하다) / use the interface(인터페이스를 사용하다) / dedicate our large brains(큰 두뇌를 바치다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
❌ ① collectively — population — essentially: (A) collectively(집단적으로)는 independently(독립적으로)와 반대 의미

det.analysis: recognize(동사) → recognizing(동명사): 전치사 for 뒤에 동명사 필요

questions.passage:
(A) As we lack the resources to compute answers independently, we distribute the computation across the <u>population</u> and solve the answer slowly, generation by generation.
(B) The <u>population</u> of bacteria in the laboratory doubled every twenty minutes under the controlled conditions.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 population의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: ④ (사회의) 사람들 전체 - (특정 지역의) 개체 수
det.analysis:
❌ ① 인구 밀도 — 인구 밀도: (A)는 밀도가 아닌 사람들 전체, (B)는 개체 수
❌ ② 특정 집단 — 특정 집단: (A)는 전체 인구, (B)는 박테리아 개체군
❌ ③ (특정 지역의) 개체 수 — (사회의) 사람들 전체: (A)(B) 의미가 뒤바뀜
✅ ④ (사회의) 사람들 전체 — (특정 지역의) 개체 수: (A) 계산을 사람들 전체에 분배, (B) 박테리아 개체 수 ←정답

questions.passage:
(A) We could <u>dedicate</u> our large brains to a small piece of a giant calculation instead of trying to hold all the information ourselves.
(B) The author decided to <u>dedicate</u> her new novel to her late grandmother, who had always encouraged her to write.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B) 두 문장에서 밑줄 친 dedicate의 의미로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.analysis:
✅ ① (시간/노력을) 바치다 — (책/작품을) 헌정하다: (A) 큰 두뇌를 작은 조각에 '바치다(전념하다)', (B) 소설을 할머니에게 '헌정하다' ←정답
❌ ② (책/작품을) 헌정하다 — (시간/노력을) 바치다: (A)(B) 의미가 뒤바뀜
❌ ③ (시간/노력을) 바치다 — (시간/노력을) 바치다: (B)는 소설을 헌정하는 맥락
❌ ④ (건물을) 봉헌하다 — (책/작품을) 헌정하다: (A)는 건물 봉헌이 아님
